claims.explanation: Nocodazole kills cells by inhibiting tubulin polymerization and blocking mitotic spindle assembly, so selectivity is driven by how much cells depend on microtubule dynamics for proliferation and survival. Lines with high mitotic/spindle gene expression and intact spindle-assembly-checkpoint signaling are most sensitive, whereas lines with high drug efflux, low proliferation, or resistance mutations in tubulin or checkpoint genes are protected.

features.basis: Mitotic kinase; high expression marks proliferative, spindle-dependent cells; nocodazole response shows AURKA upregulation
Mitotic CDK; high expression indicates active cell cycle and dependence on spindle function
Mitotic topoisomerase required for chromosome segregation; nocodazole blocks its mitotic requirement
Mitotic ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme; high expression marks proliferative, spindle-dependent lines
Tubulin mutations can reduce nocodazole binding and confer resistance
Drug efflux pump; high expression reduces intracellular nocodazole
Autophagy regulator; nocodazole-induced upregulation may promote survival under microtubule stress
MAPK phosphatase; upregulation may blunt stress-induced death signaling
Oncogenic growth factor receptor; high expression can sustain survival signaling during mitotic arrest
Loss of p53 can allow mitotic slippage and survival after spindle damage
Spindle assembly checkpoint kinase; intact checkpoint prolongs mitotic arrest and promotes nocodazole lethality
Metastasis-associated chromatin modifier; downregulation in responsive line suggests high expression supports survival
